title: Fence Calculator
metaDescription: Estimate wood fence posts, rails, pickets, and bags of post-setting concrete in US units, using Quikrete's 3x-wide hole rule with a frost-depth check.
secondaryKeywords: how many fence posts do i need
how much concrete per fence post
how many pickets per 8 foot section
intent: Estimate posts, rails, pickets, and post-setting concrete for a wood fence line of a given length and height.
registerRow: Keyword Register: fence calculator (Volume 3, Competition ease 3, Ad value 3, Fit 5, Priority 27)
intro: Enter your fence line, post, and picket sizes to get the posts, rails, and pickets to buy, plus the hole size and bags of concrete for every post. Post holes follow Quikrete's post-setting method, and you can push them deeper to clear your frost line.
chartTitle: What fills one post hole (cu ft): concrete, gravel base, and buried post
uniqueAddition: Per-post concrete calculator using Quikrete's 3x-diameter, 1/3-depth hole rule with the buried post volume subtracted, a frost-depth field that deepens the hole, and a minimum post length check; the donut chart splits one hole into concrete, gravel, and post. page.md adds a bags-per-post table by post size, post length, and bag, and a posts-and-pickets table for 50 to 200 ft.

inputs.name: fenceLength
inputs.label: Fence length
inputs.help: 10 to 1,000 ft. Total length of the fence line, gates included.

inputs.name: fenceHeight
inputs.label: Fence height
inputs.help: 3 to 8 ft. Used to check that your posts are long enough. 6 ft is a common privacy fence.

inputs.name: gates
inputs.label: Number of gates
inputs.help: Whole number, 0 to 10. Each gate opening adds one post.

inputs.name: postSpacing
inputs.label: Post spacing (on center)
inputs.help: 4 to 10 ft. 6 to 8 ft is a common rule of thumb, not a manufacturer figure. Match your rail length.

inputs.name: postSize
inputs.label: Post size
inputs.help: Sets the hole width: Quikrete's guide digs the hole 3 times the post width.

inputs.name: postLength
inputs.label: Post length
inputs.help: 5 to 12 ft, the full length of the post you buy. Quikrete's method buries 1/3 of it, so a 9 ft post stands 6 ft tall.

inputs.name: picketWidth
inputs.label: Picket width
inputs.help: 3 to 8 in. Use the actual face width: a 1x6 picket is about 5.5 in.

inputs.name: picketGap
inputs.label: Picket gap
inputs.help: -2 to 2 in. 0 for side-by-side privacy. For board-on-board, enter the overlap on each edge as a negative number (1 in overlap = -1).

inputs.name: bagType
inputs.label: Concrete bag

options.label: 80 lb Quikrete Concrete Mix (0.60 cu ft)

inputs.help: Yields come from each product's data sheet (see Sources).

inputs.name: gateWidth
inputs.label: Gate width (each)
inputs.help: 2 to 12 ft. Gate openings are taken out of the fence length before pickets and rails are counted.

inputs.name: railsPerSection
inputs.label: Rails per section
inputs.help: Horizontal rails between each pair of posts.

inputs.name: frostDepth
inputs.label: Frost depth
inputs.help: 0 to 72 in. Ask your local building department. If it is deeper than 1/3 of the post, the post is buried to this depth instead.

inputs.name: picketWaste
inputs.label: Picket waste
inputs.help: 0 to 15%. Extra pickets for splits, bad boards, and cuts. 5% is our starting estimate, not a manufacturer figure.

outputs.name: minPostLength
outputs.label: Shortest post for your fence height

sources.title: QUIKRETE Setting Posts project guide (The Quikrete Companies): hole 3 times the post width, 1/3 of the post buried, 6 in gravel base
QUIKRETE Fast-Setting Concrete Mix, Product No. 1004 data sheet (The Quikrete Companies): yields of 0.375 cu ft (50 lb) and 0.45 cu ft (60 lb)
QUIKRETE Concrete Mix, Product No. 1101 data sheet (The Quikrete Companies): yield of 0.60 cu ft per 80 lb bag
